title: Agentic AI vs. generative AI: Key differences for B2B support | Pylon
summary: Learn about the differences between agentic AI versus generative AI. Understand the use cases, risks, and how each can improve customer support workflows.
body_markdown:
If a customer reports failed API requests, you might need help with more than the reply. Someone has to check the error, understand the account’s setup, choose the best solution, and decide whether to involve the dev team. A well-written answer only helps once you have enough evidence to explain the problem and present a fix.


Both[agentic AI](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/agentic-ai-use-cases) and generative AI (GenAI) offer tools to streamline your support workflows. GenAI can turn information into a useful response, while agentic AI can pursue an investigation across tools and choose steps within limits you set. Each model uses LLMs, and you can combine them in the same processes.


In this article, we’ll explain the similarities and differences between agentic AI versus generative AI. And we’ll discuss how you can apply these technologies to[build stronger customer relationships](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-build-relationship-with-customers) .


## What’s agentic AI vs. generative AI?


Ask AI view from Pylon


GenAI creates or transforms content, while agentic AI works toward a goal, using feedback to decide what to do next. These types of AI can also work in combination: An agent could use a generative model to interpret your request, then select a tool for investigation and explain its findings.


Here’s what each technology can offer for your support workflows.


Factor Generative AI Agentic AI


Purpose Produce content, like a summary or draft Pursue an outcome, like investigating an issue


Autonomy Generates an output within the surrounding workflow Can choose and carry out steps within assigned limits


Prompts Instructions describe the output you want Instructions define the goal and boundaries


Decision making Can produce analysis or recommendations Uses decisions to determine the next step


Tool use Applications can supply retrieved data or connected tools Selects available tools as the task progresses


Multistep execution A person or predefined workflow can sequence generation tasks Can revise its next step based on earlier results


Human oversight Review content before relying on or publishing it Review evidence, action permissions, and escalation points

## Examples of agentic AI and generative AI in customer support


Let’s take a closer look at how these two types of AI, generative and agentic, can be useful in a[B2B customer support context](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/what-is-b2b-customer-service-definition-best-practices-examples) .


### GenAI for day-to-day support tasks


Once you’ve established the cause of an issue, GenAI can turn your technical notes into a[clear customer explanation](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-for-customer-experience) . Just give your model the verified findings and approved troubleshooting steps, then let it know what level of detail your customer needs.


Once the draft is ready, you can make sure it preserves the facts and uses the right tone before you send it. The same technology can summarize a long issue for your dev team or turn a resolved question into an[article draft](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/knowledge-base-articles-what-they-are-how-to-make-them-effective) .


### Agentic AI for cross-tool support workflows


If the cause of an issue is unknown, your agentic support workflow can step in to gather evidence. With the right tools and context enabled, an AI agent could retrieve the latest error to compare it with known issues, and check the account configuration.


If the agent finds a matching engineering issue, that could lead to an escalation with evidence attached. An unfamiliar error could mean you need more information from the customer. At that point, the agent could use GenAI to draft the appropriate message, while your team reviews consequential actions.


### How to put both types of AI to work


To start adding AI into your support workflows, start with one simple and repeatable task. If a summary or suggested reply is all you need, GenAI could be enough. Add agentic steps when they remove investigation work or rote tasks your team would otherwise handle manually.


Before you[set up an AI agent](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-set-up-ai-agents) , clearly define the evidence it should return and where it should stop. Test past issues, then compare human effort, results, corrections, and escalations with your current process to see if AI is making a true difference.

[Pylon’s approach to agentic support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/pylon-becomes-the-agentic-support-platform) keeps your team focused on directing investigations and reviewing outcomes. All AI agents work with shared customer context, but each type has a different role in moving issues forward:

Replies use public, customer-agnostic knowledge your team has approved. Private account details and internal conversations stay separate from those answers, even when they inform the investigation.


## Risks and limitations of generative and agentic AI


Agent runbook view from Pylon


One of the biggest risks when using any type of AI is trusting an answer that sounds correct. GenAI can invent details and reflect biases, and its explanation may not show how it reached that conclusion.


An agent that uses the same base model can inherit those problems. So always ask for supporting sources, and check consequential claims against the underlying evidence. That might mean verifying an error and the affected configuration before recommending a fix.


Action permissions add operational risk, because a mistaken conclusion could cause an incorrect change in a live system. Retrieved material can also contain instructions that redirect the agent, creating security and privacy problems.


To reduce these risks, limit the AI’s access. Keep sensitive findings internal, and add review checkpoints before consequential changes. Assign someone to correct mistakes and monitor escalations. Otherwise, automation can move an issue forward while no one checks to see whether the customer’s problem was[resolved to their satisfaction](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-satisfaction-ratings) .

## FAQ


### What are the four types of generative AI output?


Four common GenAI output categories are text, image, audio, and video. Many models can also generate code and combine multiple formats into complex outputs.


### Is agentic AI better than generative AI?


Which AI technology is best, agentic AI or generative AI, depends on the task you need it to perform. Generative AI may be enough for a proposed draft or a summary of existing information. Agentic AI fits work that requires investigation and decisions across multiple steps, provided you can supply reliable tools and appropriate oversight.


### What are the top three AI agents?


Pylon’s Assist Agent, Automations, and Support Agent are three examples of agentic AI that can improve B2B customer support. These agents offer direct assistance for your team, trigger work based on defined workflows, and even handle some customer-facing resolutions autonomously.


### Does agentic AI require human oversight?


Agentic AI performs best with human oversight. You’ll want to carefully define the AI’s scope and review its overall performance, even when individual steps run automatically. Built-in human review checkpoints can pause a workflow for your review before the AI continues.
